claim: TcMAC21 mice carry a non-mosaic and independently segregating mouse artificial chromosome with a near-complete copy of the long arm of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21q).
source: TcMAC21 mice carry a non-mosaic and independently segregating mouse artificial chromosome with a near-complete copy of the long arm of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21q) (Kazuki et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kazuki et al., 2020

claim: The Hsa21q in TcMAC21 is comprised of approximately 37 Mb and 199 protein-coding genes.
source: The Hsa21q in TcMAC21 is comprised of ~37 Mb and 199 PCGs (Figure 1A).
evidence: Supported by reference to Figure 1A showing the chromosome structure

claim: Hsa21-derived transcripts are differentially expressed and regulated in a tissue-specific manner in TcMAC21 mice.
source: RNA-sequencing showed that TcMAC21 mice are capable of expressing Hsa21-derived transcripts in each of the tissues examined, and that gene expression is regulated in a tissue-specific manner.
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data presented in the manuscript

claim: There are three large regions of Hsa21 with little or no transcription activity in TcMAC21 mice: 29.5–31.1 Mb, 44.5–44.8 Mb, and 45.3–46.2 Mb.
source: There are three large regions of Hsa21 with little or no transcription activity: 29.5–31.1 Mb, 44.5–44.8 Mb, and 45.3–46.2 Mb.
evidence: Supported by transcriptional activity mapping data

claim: gWAT expresses 115 human protein-coding genes while iWAT expresses only 27.
source: gWAT expresses 115 human PCGs while iWAT expresses only 27.
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data comparing tissue expression profiles

claim: Of the 126 Hsa21-derived protein-coding genes expressed by at least one tissue, a majority (65 total) are shared between BAT, gWAT, liver, and skeletal muscle.
source: Of the 126 Hsa21-derived PCGs expressed by at least one tissue, a majority (65 total) are shared between BAT, gWAT, liver, and skeletal muscle.
evidence: Supported by overlap analysis shown in Figure 1D

claim: TcMAC21 pups are born at the same weight as their euploid littermates.
source: As previously documented, TcMAC21 pups are born at the same weight as their euploid littermates (Kazuki et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kazuki et al., 2020

claim: By 3 months of age, TcMAC21 mice fed a standard chow weighed significantly less (~8.5 g) than euploid littermates.
source: However, by 3 months of age TcMAC21 mice fed a standard chow weighed significantly less (~8.5 g) than euploid littermates, and this weight difference remained stable over time (Figure 2A).
evidence: Supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 2A

claim: TcMAC21 mice have significantly reduced absolute and relative fat mass compared to euploid controls.
source: Body composition analysis showed that TcMAC21 have significantly reduced absolute and relative (normalized to body weight) fat mass (Figure 2B).
evidence: Supported by body composition analysis data in Figure 2B

claim: The weight differences in TcMAC21 mice were not due to reduced plasma IGF-1 and growth hormone, as their circulating levels were higher in TcMAC21 compared to euploid mice.
source: The size and body weight differences were not due to reduced plasma IGF-1 and growth hormone, as their circulating levels were in fact higher in TcMAC21 compared to euploid mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by hormone measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: TcMAC21 mice consumed the same or slightly higher amount of food despite being markedly leaner than euploid controls.
source: Differences in body weight were not due to reduced caloric intake, as TcMAC21 mice actually consumed the same or slightly higher amount of food despite being markedly leaner (Figure 2C and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by food intake measurements in Figure 2C

claim: TcMAC21 mice were expending approximately 25% more energy and were significantly more active compared to euploid controls.
source: Indirect calorimetry analysis indicated that TcMAC21 mice—regardless of the photocycle (light or dark phase) and metabolic states (ad libitum fed, fasting, refeed)—were expending ~25% more energy and were significantly more active compared to euploid controls (Figure 2D–F and Supplementary file 2).
evidence: Supported by indirect calorimetry data in Figures 2D-F

claim: Hyperactivity and elevated energy expenditure in TcMAC21 mice were not due to altered circulating thyroid hormones.
source: Hyperactivity and elevated EE were not due to altered circulating thyroid hormones, as serum triiodothyronine (T3, the active form of TH) levels were not different between chow fed TcMAC21 and euploid mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by thyroid hormone measurements in Figure 2—figure supplement 1

claim: TcMAC21 mice had significantly smaller adipocyte cell size in both subcutaneous (inguinal) and visceral (gonadal) fat depots.
source: In accordance with the lean phenotype, TcMAC21 mice had significantly smaller adipocyte cell size in both subcutaneous (inguinal) and visceral (gonadal) fat depots (Figure 2G–H)
evidence: Supported by histological analysis in Figures 2G-H

claim: TcMAC21 mice had significantly reduced fat accumulation in liver.
source: as well as significantly reduced fat accumulation in liver (Figure 2I).
evidence: Supported by liver histology in Figure 2I

claim: Fasting blood glucose was significantly lower in TcMAC21 mice compared to euploid controls.
source: Although fasting insulin levels were not different between groups, fasting blood glucose was significantly lower in TcMAC21 mice (Figure 2K).
evidence: Supported by glucose measurements in Figure 2K

claim: TcMAC21 mice showed modest improvements in insulin sensitivity compared to euploid mice.
source: The insulin resistance index (homeostatic model assessment for insulin resistance [HOMA-IR]) along with GTT and insulin tolerance test (ITT) suggested modest improvements in insulin sensitivity in TcMAC21 relative to euploid mice (Figure 2L–N).
evidence: Supported by HOMA-IR, GTT, and ITT data in Figures 2L-N

claim: After 8 weeks on high-fat diet, TcMAC21 mice gained only approximately 3 g of body weight, whereas euploid controls gained more than 15 g.
source: Indeed, after 8 weeks on high-fat diet (HFD), TcMAC21 mice gained only ~3 g of body weight, whereas the euploid controls gained >15 g of body weight over the same period.
evidence: Supported by body weight measurements over time on HFD

claim: TcMAC21 mice weighed approximately 50% less than euploid controls after 8 weeks on high-fat diet.
source: Consequently, TcMAC21 mice weighed ~50% less than euploid controls (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by body weight data in Figure 3A

claim: The lean phenotype seen in HFD-fed TcMAC21 is largely due to reduced adiposity.
source: Because relative lean mass was higher in TcMAC21 compared to euploid mice (Figure 3B), the lean phenotype seen in HFD-fed TcMAC21 is largely due to reduced adiposity.
evidence: Supported by body composition analysis in Figure 3B

claim: Fasting glucose and insulin levels, and the insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR), were markedly lower in TcMAC21 mice relative to euploid controls.
source: Fasting glucose and insulin levels, and the insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR), were markedly lower in TcMAC21 mice relative to euploid controls (Figure 3G–H), indicative of enhanced insulin sensitivity.
evidence: Supported by metabolic measurements in Figures 3G-H

claim: During glucose tolerance tests, the amount of serum insulin present was dramatically lower in TcMAC21 compared to euploid mice.
source: In glucose tolerance tests (GTTs), even though the rate of glucose disposal was similar between TcMAC21 and euploid mice, the amount of serum insulin present during GTT (time 0, 15, and 30 min) was dramatically lower in TcMAC21 (Figure 3I–J).
evidence: Supported by GTT and insulin measurements in Figures 3I-J

claim: TcMAC21 mice exhibited higher insulin sensitivity as indicated by significant differences in insulin-stimulated glucose disposal during insulin tolerance tests.
source: Indeed, when we directly assessed insulin action via ITTs, TcMAC21 mice clearly exhibited higher insulin sensitivity as indicated by the significant differences in insulin-stimulated glucose disposal (Figure 3K).
evidence: Supported by ITT data in Figure 3K

claim: The insulin response to food intake in TcMAC21 mice was strikingly smaller in magnitude compared to euploid controls during fasting-refeeding.
source: Under this fasting-refeeding condition, we could clearly see the resumption of food intake was successful at increasing blood glucose in TcMAC21 (Figure 3L); however, the insulin response to food intake in TcMAC21 mice was strikingly smaller in magnitude compared to euploid controls (Figure 3M).
evidence: Supported by fasting-refeeding data in Figures 3L-M

claim: Quantification of β-islet size, pancreatic insulin and somatostatin content, as well as insulin granule and vesicle size did not reveal any intrinsic differences between TcMAC21 and euploid mice.
source: Quantification of β-islet size, pancreatic insulin and SST content, as well as insulin granule and vesicle size did not reveal any intrinsic differences between TcMAC21 and euploid mice (Figure 3N–Q), thus ruling out a developmental cause and arguing in favor of enhanced insulin action.
evidence: Supported by pancreatic analysis in Figures 3N-Q

claim: Neither fecal frequency, average fecal pellet weight, nor fecal energy content was different between TcMAC21 and euploid mice.
source: Neither fecal frequency, average fecal pellet weight, nor fecal energy content was different between TcMAC21 and euploid mice (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by fecal analysis data in Figure 4B

claim: Both serum T3 (the active form) and T4 (precursor of T3) levels were significantly higher in HFD-fed TcMAC21 relative to euploid mice housed at room temperature.
source: Both serum T3 (the active form) and T4 (precursor of T3) levels were significantly higher in TcMAC21 relative to euploid mice (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by thyroid hormone measurements in Figure 4C

claim: T3 hormone was not elevated in HFD-fed mice housed at thermoneutrality (30°C).
source: T3 hormone, however, was not elevated in HFD-fed mice housed at thermoneutrality (30°C) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by thyroid hormone measurements at thermoneutrality

claim: Deep colon temperatures of TcMAC21 were elevated, most notably in the dark cycle when mice are active.
source: Indeed, deep colon temperatures of TcMAC21 were elevated, most notably in the dark cycle when mice are active (Figure 4G).
evidence: Supported by temperature measurements in Figure 4G

claim: Thermal imaging showed an elevated skin temperature around the interscapular region of TcMAC21 mice.
source: Assessment with thermal imaging showed an elevated skin temperature around the interscapular region of TcMAC21 mice, whereas the tail skin temperature was not different between groups (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: Supported by thermal imaging data in Figures 4G-H

claim: The differences in interscapular skin temperatures persisted in TcMAC21 even when compared to weight-matched wild-type mice.
source: Importantly, the differences in interscapular skin temperatures persisted in TcMAC21 even when compared to weight-matched wild-type mice (Figure 4I–J), thus ruling out body weight (and hence surface area/volume ratio) as the cause of greater heat generation to compensate for greater heat loss.
evidence: Supported by comparison with weight-matched controls in Figures 4I-J

claim: Elevated body temperature was not observed in chow-fed TcMAC21 mice.
source: Elevated body temperature, however, was not observed in chow-fed mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), even though chow-fed TcMAC21 were also hyperactive and had higher EE.
evidence: Supported by temperature measurements in chow-fed mice

claim: Histological analysis of the interscapular BAT revealed a marked reduction in fat accumulation and a 'healthy' brown appearance in TcMAC21 mice when compared to euploid controls.
source: Consistent with the thermal imaging data, histological analysis of the interscapular BAT revealed a marked reduction in fat accumulation and a 'healthy' brown appearance in TcMAC21 mice when compared to euploid controls (Figure 4K–L)
evidence: Supported by BAT histology in Figures 4K-L

claim: There were minimal differences in key thermogenic and fat oxidation genes in BAT between TcMAC21 and euploid mice.
source: Surprisingly, we found minimal differences in key thermogenic and fat oxidation genes between the two groups of mice (Figure 4M, Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by gene expression analysis in Figure 4M and Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: The transcriptomes of BAT, liver, gWAT, and iWAT in TcMAC21 were remarkably similar to euploid controls, with only a limited number of genes whose expression was significantly altered.
source: Again, to our surprise and contrary to expectation, we found the transcriptomes of BAT, liver, gWAT, and iWAT in TcMAC21 to be remarkably similar to euploid controls, with only a limited number of genes whose expression was significantly altered (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data in Figures 5A-D

claim: There was not a single tissue that had more than 0.3% of its transcriptome (mouse) significantly altered.
source: There was not a single tissue that had more than 0.3% of its transcriptome (mouse) significantly altered (Figure 5E and Supplementary files 6-9).
evidence: Supported by transcriptome analysis summary in Figure 5E

claim: RNA-sequencing of TcMAC21 skeletal muscle (gastrocnemius) revealed it to be the most transcriptionally dynamic tissue, with 4.2% of the transcriptome changed relative to euploid controls.
source: RNA-sequencing of TcMAC21 skeletal muscle (gastrocnemius) revealed it to be the most transcriptionally dynamic tissue, with 4.2% of the transcriptome changed relative to euploid controls (Figure 6A).
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data in Figure 6A

claim: Within the skeletal muscle of TcMAC21, there were 432 upregulated genes and 501 downregulated genes.
source: Within the skeletal muscle of TcMAC21, there were 432 upregulated genes and 501 downregulated genes (Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and Supplementary file 10).
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: Gene Ontology analysis of the differentially expressed genes highlighted upregulated pathways related to thermogenesis, mitochondrial activity, and amino acid metabolism.
source: Gene Ontology analysis of the differentially expressed genes (DEGs) highlighted upregulated pathways related to thermogenesis, mitochondrial activity, and amino acid metabolism; and downregulated pathways related to TGF-β, insulin, growth hormone, calcium, adrenergic, serine/threonine kinase, and cGMP-PKG signaling pathways (Figure 6B).
evidence: Supported by Gene Ontology analysis in Figure 6B

claim: The most notable upregulated gene with the biggest magnitude of change in skeletal muscle was Sln (encoding sarcolipin).
source: While a few of the genes were significantly different in expression, the most notable upregulated gene with the biggest magnitude of change was Sln (Figure 6C), encoding the 31 amino acid single-pass membrane protein, SLN.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data in Figure 6C

claim: SLN is a regulator and an uncoupler of the sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum calcium ATPase (SERCA).
source: SLN is a regulator and an uncoupler of the sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum calcium ATPase (SERCA) (Bal and Periasamy, 2020; Wang et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bal and Periasamy, 2020 and Wang et al., 2021

claim: When SLN binds to SERCA, it promotes Ca2+ slippage without affecting the ATPase activity of the pump.
source: When SLN binds to SERCA, it promotes Ca2+ slippage without affecting the ATPase activity of the pump; therefore, more ATP needs to be consumed by the SERCA pump to re-sequester Ca2+ back into SR in the presence of SLN.
evidence: Supported by citations to Smith et al., 2002 and Sahoo et al., 2013

claim: SLN uncouples ATP hydrolysis from calcium transport into the SR, resulting in futile SERCA pump activity, ATP hydrolysis, and heat generation.
source: Effectively, SLN uncouples ATP hydrolysis from calcium transport into the SR (Smith et al., 2002; Sahoo et al., 2013). This results in futile SERCA pump activity, ATP hydrolysis, and heat generation (Wang et al., 2021; Bal et al., 2012; Mall et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations describing SLN mechanism

claim: Regardless of diet (chow or HFD) and temperature (22°C or 30°C), TcMAC21 mice consistently had approximately 20- to 30-fold upregulated Sln expression.
source: Interestingly, regardless of diet (chow or HFD) and temperature (22°C or 30°C), TcMAC21 mice consistently had ~20- to 30-fold upregulated Sln expression (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data across conditions in Figure 6E

claim: SLN protein levels were strikingly upregulated in TcMAC21 skeletal muscle (gastrocnemius).
source: Consistent with the mRNA data, SLN protein levels were also strikingly upregulated in TcMAC21 skeletal muscle (gastrocnemius) (Figure 6F–G).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data in Figures 6F-G

claim: The SLN protein levels in TcMAC21 were approximately 4.5-fold higher than the euploid mice.
source: While the transgenic mouse had ~2.5-fold higher level of SLN compared to controls, the SLN protein levels in TcMAC21 were ~4.5-fold higher than the euploid mice (Figure 6G).
evidence: Supported by Western blot quantification in Figure 6G

claim: Immunofluorescence indicated substantially more SLN positive muscle fibers in TcMAC21 mice.
source: Immunofluorescence also indicated substantially more SLN positive muscle fibers in TcMAC21 mice (Figure 6H–I).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figures 6H-I

claim: None of the genes involved in muscle repair, wasting, and atrophy were significantly upregulated in TcMAC21 mice.
source: However, none of the genes involved in muscle repair, wasting, and atrophy were significantly upregulated (Supplementary file 11), suggesting that Sln overexpression is not due to structural or functional deficit of the skeletal muscle in TcMAC21 mice.
evidence: Supported by gene expression analysis in Supplementary file 11

claim: The average gastrocnemius muscle fiber cross-sectional area in TcMAC21 was significantly smaller compared to euploid mice.
source: Quantification of histological sections revealed that the average gastrocnemius muscle fiber CSA in TcMAC21 was significantly smaller compared to euploid mice (Figure 6J and Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by histological quantification in Figure 6J

claim: Protein levels of mitochondrial complexes I–V were significantly higher in TcMAC21 gastrocnemius muscle compared to euploid controls.
source: In accordance, protein levels of mitochondrial complexes I–V were significantly higher in TcMAC21 gastrocnemius muscle compared to euploid controls (Figure 6K–L).
evidence: Supported by Western blot data in Figures 6K-L

claim: Immunofluorescence showed substantially higher succinate dehydrogenase (SDHB) staining in gastrocnemius muscle of TcMAC21 mice.
source: Corroborating the Western blot data, immunofluorescence also showed substantially higher succinate dehydrogenase (SDHB) staining (marker of oxidative capacity) in gastrocnemius muscle of TcMAC21 mice (Figure 6M–N).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figures 6M-N

claim: Most muscle types from TcMAC21 fed either chow or HFD showed significantly elevated oxygen consumption due to elevated mitochondrial respiration.
source: Except soleus and heart, most muscle types from TcMAC21 fed either chow or HFD—regardless of whether they were predominantly slow-twitch (oxidative), fast-twitch (glycolytic), or mixed—showed significantly elevated oxygen consumption due to elevated mitochondrial respiration (Figure 6O–Q and Figure 6—figure supplements 4–9).
evidence: Supported by respirometry data in Figure 6O-Q and supplementary figures

claim: Enhanced mitochondrial complex I, II, and IV activities were more pronounced in glycolytic muscle tissues.
source: Enhanced mitochondrial complex I, II, and IV activities were more pronounced in glycolytic muscle tissues, suggesting that these normally glycolytic muscle fibers may assume a more oxidative phenotype in TcMAC21 mice.
evidence: Supported by respirometry data showing differential effects across muscle types

claim: Mitochondrial activities of complexes I and II in interscapular BAT was largely unchanged in TcMAC21.
source: In contrast to muscle, mitochondrial activities of complexes I and II in interscapular BAT was largely unchanged in TcMAC21 (Figure 6Q and Figure 6—figure supplement 6)
evidence: Supported by respirometry data in Figure 6Q and Figure 6—figure supplement 6

claim: Mitochondrial complex I, II, and IV activity was markedly reduced in the liver and heart of both chow- and HFD-fed TcMAC21 compared to euploid mice.
source: Unexpectedly and in striking contrast to muscle and BAT, mitochondrial complex I, II, and IV activity was markedly reduced in the liver and heart of both chow- and HFD-fed TcMAC21 compared to euploid mice (Figure 6Q and Figure 6—figure supplements 7–8)
evidence: Supported by respirometry data in Figure 6Q and supplementary figures

claim: When housed at thermoneutrality (30°C), TcMAC21 mice consumed a similar amount of calories as the euploid controls but maintained their lean phenotypes with lower fasting insulin levels.
source: When housed at thermoneutrality (30°C), TcMAC21 mice consumed a similar amount of calories as the euploid controls but maintained their lean phenotypes with lower fasting insulin levels (Figure 7A–E).
evidence: Supported by metabolic measurements at thermoneutrality in Figures 7A-E

claim: TcMAC21 mice housed at thermoneutrality had smaller adipocyte cell size and lower lipid contents in BAT and liver.
source: Consistent with lower adiposity, TcMAC21 mice housed at thermoneutrality had smaller adipocyte cell size and lower lipid contents in BAT and liver (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis in Figure 7—figure supplement 1

claim: RNA-sequencing on skeletal muscle from HFD-fed TcMAC21 housed at thermoneutrality showed a total of 113 differentially expressed genes, with 59 being upregulated and 54 being downregulated.
source: RNA-sequencing data showed a total of 113 DEGs in the skeletal muscle of TcMAC21 mice, with 59 being upregulated and 54 being downregulated (Figure 8A and Supplementary file 14).
evidence: Supported by RNA-sequencing data in Figure 8A

claim: There were 81 genes differentially expressed by TcMAC21 at both 22°C and 30°C temperatures, with 37 upregulated and 44 downregulated.
source: Notably, there were 81 genes differentially expressed by TcMAC21 at both temperatures, with 37 upregulated (all PCGs) and 44 downregulated (43 PCGs and 1 NPCG) genes.
evidence: Supported by comparative RNA-sequencing analysis across temperatures

claim: Five genes were identified as potential Sln regulators that remained unchanged at both 22°C and 30°C in TcMAC21 skeletal muscle: A930018M24Rik (upregulated), Csde1, Kmt5a, Vasp, and Calm1 (downregulated).
source: We next sorted the data by p-value, then compared the entire list of unchanged transcripts to the list of shared DEGs shown in Figure 8B, and found that only five genes were present in both (Figure 8C). This list contains one upregulated gene (A930018M24Rik) and four downregulated PCGs (Csde1, Kmt5a, Vasp, and Calm1).
evidence: Supported by comparative analysis in Figure 8C

claim: There was a total of 106 human transcripts expressed by TcMAC21 mice housed at 22°C and 30°C, with 94 protein-coding genes and 12 non-protein-coding genes.
source: There was a total of 106 human transcripts expressed by TcMAC21 mice housed at 22°C and 30°C, with 94 PCGs and 12 NPCGs (Figure 8D).
evidence: Supported by human transcript analysis in Figure 8D

claim: A majority (75 out of 83) of the human genes that were turned off at 30°C are non-protein-coding genes.
source: Interestingly, a majority (75 out of 83) of the human genes that were turned off at 30°C are NPCGs.
evidence: Supported by analysis of temperature-dependent gene expression

claim: The presence of an extra chromosome in mammals is generally lethal during fetal development, due to widespread cellular havoc caused by misregulated gene expression arising from gene dosage imbalance.
source: The presence of an extra chromosome in mammals is generally lethal during fetal development, due to widespread cellular havoc caused by misregulated gene expression arising from gene dosage imbalance (Zhu et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhu et al., 2018

claim: Down syndrome (DS), resulting from trisomy of chromosome 21, is one of the rare aneuploidies compatible with life although as many as 80% of trisomy 21 conceptuses miscarry.
source: Down syndrome (DS), resulting from trisomy of chromosome 21, is one of the rare aneuploidies compatible with life although as many as 80% of trisomy 21 conceptuses miscarry (Antonarakis et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Antonarakis et al., 2020

claim: The increased expression of approximately 500 transcribed sequences of human chromosome 21 affects many cell types and organ systems during development and in the postnatal period.
source: The increased expression of ~500 transcribed sequences of human chromosome 21 (Hsa21) affects many cell types and organ systems during development and in the postnatal period (Korenberg et al., 1994; Antonarakis, 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Korenberg et al., 1994 and Antonarakis, 2017

claim: Adolescents and adults with DS have an increased incidence of obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes.
source: In addition to developmental abnormalities associated with DS, there is an increasing awareness that adolescents and adults with DS also have an increased incidence of obesity, insulin resistance, and diabetes (Van Goor et al., 1997; Bertapelli et al., 2016; Fonseca et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Van Goor et al., 1997; Bertapelli et al., 2016; Fonseca et al., 2005

claim: The segmental trisomic Ts65Dn mouse contains only approximately 55% of the orthologous protein-coding genes found on Hsa21.
source: However, the segmental trisomic Ts65Dn mouse contains only ~55% of the orthologous protein-coding genes (PCGs) found on Hsa21 (Gupta et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gupta et al., 2016

claim: Ts65Dn mouse contains additional trisomic genes from the centromeric region of mouse chromosome 17 (Mmu17) not found in Hsa21.
source: In addition, it contains additional trisomic genes from the centromeric region of mouse chromosome 17 (Mmu17) not found in Hsa21, thus complicating the genotype-phenotype relationships (Duchon et al., 2011; Reinholdt et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citations to Duchon et al., 2011 and Reinholdt et al., 2011

claim: Tc1 mice are missing more than 50 of the 220 protein-coding genes on Hsa21 due to deletion and mutations.
source: However, Tc1 mice are missing >50 of the 220 PCGs on Hsa21 due to deletion and mutations (Gribble et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gribble et al., 2013

claim: Tc1 mice show extensive mosaicism (i.e. the human chromosome is present in zygotes but is lost randomly from cells during development).
source: In addition, Tc1 mice show extensive mosaicism (i.e. the human chromosome is present in zygotes but is lost randomly from cells during development).
evidence: Supported by established knowledge about Tc1 mice

claim: TcMAC21 is not mosaic and contains 93% of HSA21q protein-coding genes, and is considered the most representative mouse model of DS.
source: TcMAC21 is not mosaic and contains 93% of HSA21q PCGs, and is considered the most representative mouse model of DS.
evidence: Supported by description of TcMAC21 model characteristics

claim: Both mouse and rat that carry a non-mosaic Hsa21 recapitulate many DS phenotypes related to the central nervous system, craniofacial skeleton, and heart.
source: Both mouse and rat that carry a non-mosaic Hsa21 recapitulate many DS phenotypes related to the central nervous system (e.g. reduced cerebellum volume, learning and memory deficit), craniofacial skeleton, and heart (Kazuki et al., 2020; Kazuki et al., 2022).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kazuki et al., 2020 and Kazuki et al., 2022

claim: SLN-mediated futile SERCA activity in skeletal muscle is a potential driver underlying the hypermetabolism phenotypes seen in TcMAC21 mice.
source: All together, these data suggest that SLN-mediated futile SERCA activity in skeletal muscle is a potential driver underlying the hypermetabolism phenotypes seen in TcMAC21 mice.
evidence: Supported by integration of multiple experimental findings

claim: The futile SERCA pump activity consumes more ATP to transport Ca2+ into SR due to Ca2+ slippage, creating a huge energy demand and markedly driving up the activity of mitochondrial respiration.
source: Because the futile SERCA pump activity consumes more ATP to transport Ca2+ into SR due to Ca2+ slippage (Wang et al., 2021; Smith et al., 2002; Sahoo et al., 2013; Mall et al., 2006; Sahoo et al., 2015), this creates a huge energy demand and markedly drives up the activity of mitochondrial respiration to supply the ATP needed for the SERCA pump.
evidence: Supported by citations describing SERCA mechanism and inference from data

claim: Elevated mitochondrial respiration results in systemic channeling of metabolic substrates (e.g. lipids) into skeletal muscle to fuel the elevated mitochondrial respiration rate.
source: Presumably, this effect results in systemic channeling of metabolic substrates (e.g. lipids) into skeletal muscle to fuel the elevated mitochondrial respiration rate.
evidence: Based on inference from observed metabolic changes

claim: The systemic channeling of metabolic substrates leads to secondary improvements and protection—reduced fat accumulation and smaller adipocytes—observed in liver, BAT, gWAT, and iWAT despite minimal changes in the transcriptomes of these tissues.
source: This in turn leads to secondary improvements and protection—reduced fat accumulation and smaller adipocytes—we observed in liver, BAT, gWAT, and iWAT despite minimal changes in the transcriptomes of these tissues.
evidence: Based on inference from observed tissue changes and transcriptome data

claim: Thyroid hormone (T3) is likely not the driver of SLN overexpression since serum T3 was not different between TcMAC21 and euploid housed at thermoneutrality.
source: Thyroid hormone (T3) is likely not the driver of SLN overexpression since serum T3 was not different between TcMAC21 and euploid housed at thermoneutrality (Figure 2—figure supplement 1)
evidence: Based on T3 measurements at thermoneutrality and inference

claim: SLN was shown to be upregulated in hypothyroid mice compared to euthyroid controls.
source: in addition, SLN was shown to be upregulated in hypothyroid mice compared to euthyroid controls (Kaspari et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kaspari et al., 2020

claim: The study provides proof-of-concept that sarcolipin-mediated thermogenesis via uncoupling of the SERCA pump can be harnessed to promote energy expenditure and metabolic health.
source: This serendipitous discovery provides proof-of-concept that sarcolipin-mediated thermogenesis via uncoupling of the SERCA pump can be harnessed to promote energy expenditure and metabolic health.
evidence: Based on integration of all experimental findings
